notes.summary: Raw all-support envelope calculus and actual graded ideals; positivity is exactly continuity.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs raw C=D, LSC and regularization iff continuity, nonexpansiveness, integrally closed all-support J_k/factorial profiles and exact one-factor primary covariance. No increasing-limit positivity.
notes.text:
# n1. Fixed geometric domain and raw envelope calculus

Use the entire qualified G331, with its mandatory annotation, source ledger and scope. Let R be excellent local and replace it by its reduction. For a proper maximal-primary ideal a, X_a consists of ALL centred real semivaluations v with v(a)=1; prime supports below the maximal ideal are retained. This is compact Hausdorff. The independent core evaluates actual negative effective real Cartier presentations on actual primary blowups, requiring nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral curve. C is its finite continuous uniform closure; D consists of actual infima of nonempty decreasing C-nets, including bottom. G331 proves comparison with the ideal classes, rational primary-profile density, finite maximum/addition/scaling, and positive full-fibre descent. No envelope theorem is imported.

For finite continuous phi set p_C=sup{g in C:g<=phi} and p_D=sup{u in D:u<=phi}. A negative primary constant bounds both below. If u=inf g_i<=phi and epsilon>0, the increasing open sets {g_i<phi+epsilon} cover X. Compactness and directedness select one index globally. Then g_i-epsilon is a C-minorant and is at least u-epsilon. Therefore p_C=p_D=p, finite and lower semicontinuous. If p is continuous, the open sets {g>p-epsilon}, over its C-minorants, cover X; a finite maximum approximates p uniformly from below. Thus p is in C. Conversely p in D is upper semicontinuous and hence continuous. A greatest D-minorant exists exactly when p is continuous.

Define p*(x)=inf over open U containing x of sup_U p. Since phi is continuous, p<=p*<=min(phi,0). If p* is in D it is an admissible competitor, forcing p*=p; hence it is geometric exactly when p is continuous. Monotonicity and downward shifts of competitors give ||P phi-P psi||<=||phi-psi||. These are raw identities, without presuming output positivity.

There is an actual all-support graded ideal formula. For k>=1 put J_k(phi)={f in R:v(f)>=-k phi(v) for EVERY v in X}. Semivaluation axioms make this an ideal. With M>=max(0,-min phi), it contains a^ceil(kM); when the exponent is zero one can instead use a. If phi is negative somewhere, units are excluded and J_k is proper primary; if phi>=0 everywhere it is R. It is integrally closed: in a monic ideal-integrality equation for f, a violation v(f)<-k phi(v) gives a unique finite least term, namely the leading power of f, which cannot sum to zero. Quotient by the semivaluation support justifies this even for nonminimal supports. Noetherianity gives finite generation of each J_k, not of their graded algebra.

J_k J_l is contained in J_(k+l), and J_k^l in J_(kl). Consequently -v(J_(n!))/(n!) increases and has supremum p. To prove equality, approximate any C-minorant g rationally by -v(I)/s and subtract a small positive rational primary constant, realized by multiplying powers of I and a after a common denominator. This gives an admissible rational profile within any prescribed error below g. Its underlying ideal lies in the corresponding J_s; every sufficiently large factorial is divisible by s. The inclusion of powers proves its profile is below the factorial profile. Sending the error to zero proves the formula on ALL X. This pointwise increasing formula alone proves no continuity.

For another primary b, d(v)=v(b) and H(v)=v/d(v) are bounded positive continuous section data. Functions AND obstacles transport by phi_b(Hv)=phi_a(v)/d(v). G331's order bijections imply P_b(phi_b)(Hv)=P_a(phi_a)(v)/d(v), with exactly one homogeneous factor. The J_k inequalities divide by the same d, so the ideals are literally unchanged. Bounded regularization transports too: the error from replacing 1/d(y) by 1/d(x) tends uniformly to zero near x. The cocycle follows by cancelling successive ray denominators.

Nilpotents are invisible; dimension-zero local reduction has empty boundary and the unique empty envelope. Units give zero models, and neither unit nor zero ideals give a level-one section. Lower-dimensional centres, nonminimal supports, mixed zero and partial bottom remain function and conductor data. Nonprimary gauges only give partial sections and are outside these compact primary assertions.

These are mathematical draft proofs relative to G331. Artifacts: n1.md, argument.md, P12.3-paper.md and P12.3-paper.tex. Rerun: python build_delivery.py; python final_audit.py. Execution checks artifacts, not theorem correctness.

notes.summary: Decreasing D-net closure on all excellent reduced germs, proved before the energy criterion.
notes.detailedSummary: Normal zero dichotomy plus strict continuous insertion supplies an actual C representation; full normalization descent handles arbitrary reduced germs. E350 criterion follows only after membership; no increasing closure.

# n2. Actual closure under decreasing geometric nets

Use G331 and n1. Suppose u_i in D decreases, and u=inf_i u_i. On an excellent normal local domain, G331's normal zero dichotomy says that a D-function vanishing anywhere is identically zero. If u vanishes at a point, all u_i vanish there, hence u=0. Otherwise choose a nonzero u_i0. Upper semicontinuity and compactness give u_i0<=-c for a finite c>0; this includes bottom. Thus u<=-c.

For every finite continuous F>u there is q in C with u<q<F. Indeed the directed open sets {u_i<F} cover X. Choose a common tail index i>=i0. An actual C-representation g_alpha decreasing to u_i has one term g with g<F and g<-c/2 throughout X, by two compact directed covers. Let m=min(F-g)>0 and choose 0<b<1 with b||g||<m/2. Then q=(1-b)g is in C, below F, and exceeds u at every finite point by at least bc/2. At a bottom point q is finite and also exceeds u. No positive constant has been added to C.

All strict C-majorants of u contain zero and are downward directed: apply insertion to the continuous minimum of two such majorants, which need not itself be psh. Their infimum is u. For x and finite t>u(x), choose u(x)<ell<t and an open neighbourhood where u<ell. A compact-Hausdorff Urysohn cutoff supported there interpolates between ell at x and a global strict upper bound outside, giving continuous F>u with F(x)<t. The bottom case uses any finite ell<t. Insertion supplies a C-majorant whose value at x is below t. Reverse pointwise order therefore gives an ACTUAL decreasing C-net with infimum u.

For finitely many semilocal normal centres take finite products of these index sets. For arbitrary excellent reduced R, pull u_i back to its finite normalization S. Centrewise infima belong to D_S by the preceding proof. The tuple is constant on EVERY full restriction fibre, since each pulled-back term is. G331's positive D-descent puts its descent, exactly u, in D_R. This includes conductor-infinite and internal fibres; the empty case is immediate. Thus D is closed under nonempty decreasing D-nets on every excellent reduced germ. No closure under nondirected infima, finite minima, increasing limits or arbitrary nested-net flattening is asserted.

Only after proving membership use the entire qualified E350: for a decreasing E1-net, u=inf u_i is in D, and u is in E1 iff sup_i F_infinity(u_i^[n]) is finite. Its weak mixed-measure and capacity convergence then apply at their exact stated conditions. E=-F_infinity/n, with ambient top-degree n, and lower-dimensional centres retain their class/fibre constraints. The criterion is not used to manufacture membership of an increasing obstacle supremum.

Artifacts: n2.md and the complete paper. Rerun: python build_delivery.py; python final_audit.py. This is a proof using qualified grants, not an execution-derived theorem.

# n3. Regular actual primary models for excellent normal surfaces

Use G331 for the model system and evaluations. Let R be an excellent NORMAL local domain of dimension two, in any characteristic, with arbitrary residue field, including mixed characteristic. Given finitely many actual proper primary ideals, including the gauge a, their product blowup dominates each individual blowup by G331's proved invertibility argument. It is integral projective and is an isomorphism off the closed point. Normalize it; excellence makes normalization finite. The normal surface has finitely many singular points: its nonregular locus is closed by excellence and has codimension at least two. Its local completions are normal by excellence. The complete CURRENT Stacks 54.14.5 (0BGP), specifically condition (4) implying (3), therefore gives a resolution by normalized blowups. Stacks 0BGJ's normalized-blowup constructions preserve projectivity here, since finite normalization followed by blowup is projective. The centres lie over the original closed point, where the chosen model is already regular elsewhere. We obtain a regular integral projective T, isomorphic over the punctured spectrum, principalizing every chosen ideal. No SNC claim is needed.

By the complete Stacks 0AY8 proper-birational-normal lemma, Gamma(T,O_T)=R and the closed fibre is geometrically connected. Regular local rings are factorial, so the finitely many irreducible exceptional curves E_i are Cartier. They are proper integral residue-field curves. Since a O_T is an invertible primary ideal, its effective Cartier divisor is E_a=sum b_i E_i with integer b_i>0, and its support is the entire closed fibre. There are no isolated fibre points: a Cartier divisor on this regular surface has pure codimension one. These assertions use ordinary Noetherian/catenary dimension theory, not resolution in larger dimension.

Define the ACTUAL degree matrix M_ij=deg_k(O_T(E_j)|E_i), with k=R/m. It is symmetric: off-diagonal entries are sums of local intersection lengths times actual residue degrees, and diagonal symmetry is automatic. Distinct curves have nonnegative off-diagonal intersections. The connected closed fibre makes its intersection graph connected. The line bundle O_T(-E_a) pulls back the relatively ample tautological bundle on Bl_a R, so M b<=0. At least one coordinate is strict. Otherwise every E_i would contract to a point of Bl_a. But Bl_a has a fibre curve: a zero-dimensional fibre would make this projective birational map quasi-finite and finite, hence an isomorphism over normal R; that would make a invertible and principal, impossible for a proper primary ideal in dimension two by the principal ideal theorem. A curve in T dominates a fibre curve of Bl_a, on which that ample bundle has positive degree.

Put A=-M. For t_i=b_i z_i the explicit identity is
\[
t^T A t=\sum_i (A b)_i b_i z_i^2+
\sum_{i<j}(-A_{ij})b_i b_j(z_i-z_j)^2.
\]
Every term is nonnegative. Vanishing forces z constant on the connected graph and zero at a strict coordinate; thus A is positive definite. Every principal submatrix is positive definite with nonpositive off-diagonal entries, and its inverse is entrywise nonnegative. To prove the latter, solve A_J x=y>=0 and write x=x_+-x_- with disjoint nonnegative parts. Multiplying by x_- gives x_-^T y=x_-^T A_J x_+-x_-^T A_J x_-<0 if x_- is nonzero, a contradiction. Moreover A^-1 1 has all coordinates strictly positive: a zero coordinate of a nonnegative solution would give the corresponding row value <=0. M has integer entries, so this vector is rational. Clearing denominators gives integers d_i>0 with M d<0.

The effective boundary D0=sum d_i E_i therefore has O_T(-D0) of positive degree on every closed-fibre integral curve. The complete Stacks 0B5Y criterion applies to the entire proper fibre of dimension at most one, including its possible nonreduced structure and imperfect residue field. It makes the restriction ample. The complete CURRENT 30.21.4 (0D2N) makes L=O_T(-D0) relatively ample on a neighbourhood of m, hence on the whole local base. Ordinary Serre generation/coherence and relative very ampleness give a large N for which L^N is generated and defines a closed immersion by finitely many sections. Since Gamma O_T=R and L^N is an actual subsheaf of O_T, I=Gamma(T,L^N) is a finite ideal of R. It is unit off m and proper: it vanishes on the nonempty exceptional boundary, so contains no unit. Hence I is primary, and I O_T=L^N.

Choose ideal generators containing sections defining the closed immersion; enlarging the generating list preserves a closed immersion (on the opens where an original section is nonzero it is the graph of the additional ratios, and properness closes the image). In the same projective space T and Bl_I R are integral closed subschemes agreeing with the same punctured graph. In each affine chart their prime ideals are determined by vanishing on that dense graph. Both equal its scheme-theoretic closure. Thus T is ACTUALLY Bl_I R, not merely dominated by a primary blowup. The identical argument applies to every regular common refinement obtained from finitely chosen models. There is no cofinality assertion for arbitrary proper models.

Published recursive background remains disclosed: 0BGP uses the preceding surface blowup/descent lemmas and Lipman; 0AY8 uses Stein factorization; 0B5Y uses finite-surjective ampleness descent; 0D2N uses formal functions and fibre section lifting; ordinary Serre and regular-local factoriality are published background. Their deeper historical bodies are not recursively claimed freshly proved. Complete immediate bound units were read. Artifacts: n3.md, whole-source-application-ledger.md, bounded_diagnostics.py. Rerun: python bounded_diagnostics.py; python build_delivery.py. Matrix samples only diagnose the arithmetic; the universal proof is above.

notes.summary: Full surface competitor domination and greatest finite signed-profile envelope by a nef polytope.
notes.detailedSummary: Actual primary common refinement, nef Cartier pushforward, principal-matrix negativity and all-support evaluation dominate every core/C/bounded-D competitor; unbounded competitors clamp. Coordinate-max stability yields the greatest feasible vector and the full envelope.
notes.text:
# n4. Surface nef projection and the full finite obstacle envelope

Use G331, n1 and n3. Fix a regular ACTUAL primary surface model T and E_a=sum b_i E_i as constructed in n3. Let a geometric core competitor be presented by a negative effective real curve-nef Cartier divisor D' on another actual primary model. A regular common refinement T' is itself an actual primary blowup by n3. Pullback preserves actual effectivity and curve-nefness. Write mu:T'->T, and D=mu_*D'. This is a negative exceptional real Cartier divisor on regular T. For each E_i, the effective Cartier pullback mu*E_i is a nonnegative sum of proper curves contracted to R. The actual supported degree projection formula gives D.E_i=D'.mu*E_i>=0. Explicitly, on each curve component C' of D', a point image gives degree zero for the pulled-back bundle, and a curve image gives its degree multiplied by the positive function-field degree; these are precisely the coefficients of mu_*C'. Expanding D' proves the projection identity, and symmetry of actual surface Cartier intersections exchanges its two slots. This is componentwise divisor-cycle projection and the ordinary degree rule already used in G331 (complete Stacks 0AYA); it is applied to actual supported cycles before a Chow quotient. Thus D is nef over R.

F=D'-mu*D is supported only on mu-exceptional curves, since a proper birational map of normal surfaces is an isomorphism at generic codimension-one points. For such a curve C, mu*D.C=0 and F.C=D'.C>=0. The corresponding principal submatrix of the intersection matrix of T' has negative inverse by n3. If f is the coefficient vector of F, M_J f>=0 implies f<=0. Hence F is actually negative effective, not just numerically bounded. Evaluation gives h_D'<=h_D on EVERY semivaluation support. For this statement first pass to Frac(R/p), where p is the support, lift its valuation-ring morphism to the proper model from its generic point in the punctured spectrum, and evaluate Cartier local equations. Effective exceptional equations have nonnegative finite value. No map from Frac(R) into Frac(R/p) is presumed. Coefficients on E_i are exact: c_i=b_i h_D'(nu_i), where nu_i=ord_Ei/b_i.

The same projection works for any h in C. Choose actual core approximants converging uniformly to h. Their projected coefficients b_i h_j(nu_i) converge to c_i=b_i h(nu_i); coefficient order and M c>=0 survive. At a valued centre define v(E_i) from a local Cartier equation, zero if the centre is off E_i. All are finite, nonnegative, and sum b_i v(E_i)=v(a)=1, so the projected evaluations converge uniformly and h<=sum c_i v(E_i). This limit is a genuine negative effective nef real Cartier divisor on the actual primary T.

For bounded h in D use its SPECIFIED actual C-net. The same finitely many coefficients decrease to b_i h(nu_i), remain finite, and the finite evaluation sum commutes with the limit. Thus its projected nef model function again dominates h. For an unbounded competitor below an obstacle f>=-B, the actual representation max(g_alpha,-B) proves that max(h,-B) is in bounded D, still below f and at least h. This avoids any unproved closure operation.

Now let f be a finite SIGNED rational or real linear combination of finitely many primary ideal profiles and constants. Construct T by n3 for those ideals and a. Its actual exceptional Cartier representation makes
\[
f(v)=\sum_i b_i f(nu_i)v(E_i)
\]
on ALL supports. Choose B>0 with f>=-B. Consider the finite compact polytope
\[
-B b_i\le c_i\le\min(0,b_i f(nu_i)),\qquad M c\ge0.
\]
It is nonempty because c=-B b is feasible. It is stable under coordinatewise maximum: in row i choose the vector attaining the maximum ith coordinate; all other coordinates only increase, and off-diagonal entries are nonnegative. Choose a maximizer of each coordinate and take their finite maximum. This yields a greatest vector c*. Its actual negative effective nef Cartier divisor sum c*_i E_i on T evaluates to H* in the geometric core. Since every v(E_i)>=0, H*<=f everywhere. Every D-minorant, after the clamp and projection above, has a feasible vector and is at most H*. Thus H* is the FULL geometric envelope, not an envelope only among competitors already determined on T.

This proof requires neither SNC intersections nor a singular retraction. Its decisive all-support dominance is actual Cartier negativity of F on a common actual primary regular model. The finite polytope is a mathematical construction; finite vertex enumeration is separate diagnostic evidence. Artifacts: n4.md, P12.3-paper.md, bounded_diagnostics.py and reports/bounded-diagnostics.json. Rerun: python bounded_diagnostics.py; python build_delivery.py.

# n5. All continuous and upper semicontinuous surface obstacles

Use G331, E350 and n1--n4. G331's signed ideal-difference lattice is uniformly dense in all real continuous functions on X, by the all-support lattice Stone-Weierstrass argument. For an excellent normal surface approximate any finite continuous phi uniformly by signed finite ideal combinations f_j. N4 puts their FULL envelopes in C. N1's raw nonexpansive estimate makes these converge uniformly to the raw envelope of phi. Closedness of C proves P(phi) in C, hence it is the actual greatest D-minorant. This proves continuous envelopes for EVERY excellent normal local surface, arbitrary field, characteristic and mixed characteristic. The surface model depends only on the finitely chosen approximation data; no arbitrary-model cofinality is used.

The following extension applies to ANY germ already proved to have this continuous-envelope property. For an extended upper semicontinuous obstacle phi:X->[-infinity,M], M finite, let F run over all finite continuous strict majorants. They are nonempty, closed under finite minimum, and have infimum phi. For x and finite t>phi(x), choose phi(x)<ell<t, a cutoff supported in {phi<ell} equal to one at x, and a constant M'>max(M,ell). The interpolation F=chi ell+(1-chi)M' is strictly above phi and has F(x)<t, including when phi(x) is bottom. This proves the infimum assertion. Then P(F) is an ACTUAL decreasing C-net. Its infimum p is in D by definition, lies below phi, and dominates every D-minorant of phi. Thus P(phi)=p is a greatest geometric minorant. No flattening or increasing completion is involved.

If phi_i is ANY decreasing net of bounded-above upper semicontinuous obstacles with limit phi, restrict to a tail bounded above by one finite constant. N2 proves inf_i P(phi_i) in D. For every finite continuous F>phi, the open sets {phi_i<F} cover compact X; one index works globally. Hence inf_i P(phi_i)<=P(F). Taking infimum over F, and using the opposite order inequality, proves P(phi)=inf_i P(phi_i). This is the full decreasing-USC-obstacle net stability, not only stability for a selected continuous approximation.

Finite continuous outputs are bounded continuous geometric psh. General extended USC outputs are USC with an actual decreasing C representation. If the obstacle is bounded below, the output is bounded D and hence E1. Qualified E350 gives its open-exception quasicontinuity, geometric products and energy at that granted scope. For a general bounded-above extended obstacle, E1 membership is equivalent to a uniform diagonal F_infinity bound on the decreasing P(F) net, by n2 and E350. Energy has sign E=-F/n. No equation uniqueness, strict concavity or capacity-a.e. replacement for the obstacle is inferred.

Primary-gauge covariance is exactly n1's one-factor transport, including all extended outputs and stability. Idempotence on D follows from greatestness; zero and bottom are retained. Nonnormal germs require the full conductor condition proved later; these surface assertions are NORMAL assertions.

# n6. Exact published smooth specialization

Use the entire qualified G331 and n1; use n5's general majorant-net extension only after continuous envelopes have been established. The NEW published application is Boucksom--Favre--Jonsson, Valuations and plurisubharmonic singularities, at a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension at least two. The complete immediate Setting, coefficient topology, simple-modification/closed-simplex retractions, Definitions 2.1, 2.5, 2.8, Proposition 2.7, the substantive CLOSED-simplex Proposition 3.11, and ENTIRE Section 3.5 including 3.18 and the full 3.22 proof are used at those hypotheses. Recursive Hironaka principalization, usual DEL/Lazarsfeld multiplier subadditivity, smooth Izumi and ELS approximation remain disclosed published background, not new singular hypotheses or freshly reproved historical foundations.

For a bounded continuous obstacle h determined on one simple-modification complex, take the coefficientwise supremum W of nef divisors below Z(h). Clamp competitors above the nef constant -M, where -M<=h and M>0. Their finite maxima form a coefficientwise bounded increasing net; the published nef cone is weak closed and max-stable. Hence W is nef. BFJ 3.11 gives its function g, continuous on each CLOSED simplex, with canonical extension g(v)=inf_pi g(r_pi v). Coefficient bounds and rational divisorial density give -M<=g<=0 on closed faces, then on ALL semivaluations. On the determining complex g<=h; Proposition 2.7 yields g(v)<=g(r_pi v)<=h(v). Every D-minorant of h corresponds by G331 to BFJ coefficients below W, and hence is below g, first on closed faces and then through every retraction. Bottom is separate. These steps do not use an increasing closure theorem for a singular D-class.

The complete published 3.18(iii) estimate, for this determining-envelope W, with k=j+C, gives
\[
W_j\le W\le\frac{j}{j+C}W_j,
\qquad W_j=Z(L^\infty(jW))/j.
\]
C is finite and depends on the FIXED determining complex; it is not a global thinness bound. The full proof uses 3.22 to recover W from these ideals, smooth multiplier subadditivity, and thinness versus strict negativity on that complex. The unused assertion 3.18(iv) and its proof were read too. If W=0 use the unit ideal. Otherwise L^infinity(jW) contains a completed maximal-ideal power from W>=-M and is proper because W has a negative coefficient. G331 contracts it exactly to R and preserves its primary profile g_j on ALL supports. Extend the displayed coefficient inequalities by the actual closed-face continuity and all-retraction infima. They imply g_j<=g and g_j>=(1+C/j)g, so
\[
0\le g-g_j\le MC/j
\]
uniformly on the FULL compact section. Thus g is in C before using it as the positive greatest envelope.

For arbitrary finite continuous phi, approximate it uniformly by signed rational primary profiles using G331. Principalize the finitely many ideals on a common simple modification in the exact published smooth range, so each approximating obstacle is determined on a complex. N1's nonexpansive estimate and closedness of C give its envelope in C. This is exactly the published determining nef envelope and its continuous-obstacle uniform extension, with every support retained. N5 gives extended bounded-above USC envelopes and full decreasing-USC net stability in the same range. Gauge changes are n1; the DVR and empty cases are direct as in n9.

Closed-face continuity is a substantive source theorem: a finite convex function alone need not be continuous at the boundary of a closed simplex. All retractions, not only divisorial values, are required. This proof does not apply smooth multiplier estimates to singular germs, imperfect fields or positive-characteristic higher-dimensional germs. In dimension two n3--n5 already supply the arbitrary-characteristic theorem independently.

notes.text:
# n7. Full-fibre maxima and finite-cover envelopes over normal targets

Use G331 and n1--n6. Let A be an excellent normal local domain and B a finite reduced injection whose EVERY minimal component dominates A. All marked semilocal source centres and all semivaluation supports are included; no vertical component is assigned a generic degree. G331's coefficient norm construction gives a positive normalized trace for a dominating domain source, with a finite positive weight at EVERY point of the FULL restriction fibre. For several dominating components sum their generic-degree traces and normalize by the sum of their degrees. The result is continuous, preserves C and D, is a left inverse to pullback, and has positive finite weights on the full original B-fibre. These are conclusions inside G331, not a flat or defectless ramification formula.

A second, useful route explicitly constructs the fibre maximum. For one component B/P choose a finite normal field extension M/K containing its field and every embedding image, including inseparability, and let E be A's finite integral closure in M. Let G=Aut_K(M) and q=[M:K]/|G|. The coefficient norm on E, at ANY base semivaluation and ANY lift w, has measure q sum_(sigma in G) delta_(w composed with sigma). This follows by factorizing the norm polynomial, taking quotient-support Gauss coefficient minima, and then using the dense signed ideal lattice, exactly as proved in G331. Independence of that measure and its full-fibre support show that G is transitive on the ENTIRE E/A fibre, including nonminimal supports. For H in C_B, restrict to B/P, pull back to E, and take max_(sigma in G) sigma*H. It is in C_E and fibre constant over A, so positive descent gives a C_A function equal to the maximum of H on this component's full fibre. Finite maximum over the dominating components gives MH(v)=max_(rho(w)=v)H(w) in C_A. For H in D_B, use its actual decreasing C-net. Finite-fibre directedness gives max_w inf_alpha H_alpha(w)=inf_alpha max_w H_alpha(w), including bottom: simultaneous strict tests can be met at finitely many points. Therefore MH is in D_A by an actual C representation. This proof is specific to normal targets and dominating components.

For K=C or D and a finite bounded obstacle f on A, H<=rho*f implies MH<=f and H<=rho*(MH). Pullback gives the opposite inequality of competitor suprema. Consequently the UNRESTRICTED raw envelopes satisfy P_B^K(rho*f)=rho*P_A^K(f) on all supports, even before a regularity theorem. This is stronger than a merely fibre-constrained identity, within the stated normal/dominating scope.

Suppose now the marked source centres have the continuous-envelope property, proved for normal surfaces by n5 or for the exact smooth BFJ range by n6. For continuous f set U=P_B(rho*f) in C_B. Its normalized positive average p is in C_A and below f. Every target D-minorant u pulls back below U, so u<=p. Moreover rho*p is an admissible source minorant and hence rho*p<=U. On a fibre p is a positive weighted average of the finite values U(w), and is <= each of them. Each value must equal that average. Thus rho*p=U and p=P_A(f) is the greatest continuous geometric envelope. No extended-bottom average is used to force this equality. For bounded-above USC obstacles take ONE net of continuous strict majorants as in n5; its pullback infimum is a source D-envelope by greatestness against every source minorant. This proves pullback commutation and target positivity, together with the regularity, gauge and decreasing-net rules in n5.

# n8. Full conductor criterion and the all-characteristic nonnormal obstruction

Use G331, n1, n5 and n7. Let S be the finite normalization of excellent reduced R, split at ALL marked normal centres, and rho its full compact restriction quotient. At finite conductor value fibres are singleton; at infinite value their exact rule is restriction to the conductor quotient, including fibres internal to a single centre. Positive C/D descent is precisely constancy on these whole fibres. Therefore the downstairs raw envelope pulls back to the supremum of upstairs minorants which are fibre constant. An unrestricted upstairs envelope cannot be descended merely because its obstacle descends.

For finite continuous phi let p_S be the unrestricted upstairs raw envelope. The exact criterion is
\[
p_R^*\in D_R\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
p_S\hbox{ is continuous and constant on every full fibre}.
\]
To prove necessity, first show equality of constrained and unrestricted raw suprema on the finite-conductor locus. Choose B>0 with -B<=phi, and clamp an upstairs C-minorant g into [-B,0]. The ACTUAL downstairs primary ideal K_N=c+a^N gives b_N=-(B/N)v(K_N), in [-B,0], equal to -B at conductor-infinite points. Then max(g+rho*b_N,-B) is in C_S, below rho*phi and constant on every fibre, since it is -B on the entire nontrivial-fibre stratum. It descends positively. At finite conductor value b_N tends to zero, proving the desired equality. This locus is dense in each normal centre: the conductor has a regular element, every fraction-field divisorial valuation has finite value on it, and G331 proves all-support divisorial density. If p_R* is in D, n1 makes p_R continuous. Its continuous pullback u<=p_S equals p_S on this dense locus. For a net from the locus converging to any point, lower semicontinuity of p_S gives p_S<=u. Thus equality holds everywhere and yields necessity. Conversely continuous p_S belongs to C_S by n1; full-fibre constancy and positive descent make it an admissible greatest downstairs envelope. Normal continuity is a CONDITION here; n5 and n7 supply it only in their proved sectors.

For ANY field let R=k[x,y,z]_(m)/(xy), with normalization A times B, where A=k[x,z]_(x,z), B=k[y,z]_(y,z). It is the fibre product over k[z]_(z): polynomial pairs with equal residue are represented by f+g-h, and local unit denominators can be cleared by a pair whose common residue is the product of their two unit residues. Its conductor is (x)A times(y)B. The only identified boundary pair is q_A killing x, and q_B killing y, both with z-order one. Their downstairs support (x,y) is nonminimal.

The continuous strictly negative obstacle phi=-1-1/v(y), with reciprocal infinity zero, is -1 on A and -1-1/w(y) on B. On B every centred normalized w satisfies w(f)>=ord_mB(f), hence every g in D_B satisfies g(w)<=g(o_B), first on ideal profiles, then by uniform and actual decreasing limits. Since phi(o_B)=-2, every minorant is <=-2 throughout B. The unrestricted normalization envelope is the continuous tuple (-1,-2), incompatible at q_A,q_B.

For n>=1 the A-primary ideal J_n=(x^n,xz^(n-1),z^(2n)), paired with constant -2 on B, gives a fibre-compatible C tuple and hence a positive downstairs C-minorant. Write a=w(x), b=w(z), min(a,b)=1. Its A profile is -1 when a<=b; for a>b finite it is -min(1+(a-1)/n,2); at q_A it is -2. For n=1 the middle generator is literally x, avoiding 0 times infinity. Their increasing supremum is -1 on A minus q_A and -2 at q and throughout B. The obstacle on A and the universal B inequality give these exact upper bounds for EVERY D-minorant. Monomial valuations with x-weight tending to infinity and z-weight one converge to q_A on every localized polynomial, so that raw envelope is not USC. N1 rules out a greatest geometric minorant or a geometric USC regularization, although the regularization stays below phi. In fact there is no maximal minorant: a maximal member would dominate every competitor by finite maxima, and equal the non-USC supremum. Thus nonnormal conductor descent can obstruct even a bounded strictly negative obstacle with smooth normalization.

If a normalization fibre meets TWO distinct positive-dimensional normal centres, there is also a general obstruction. Choose a centred divisorial point nu on one centre with finite conductor value; its downstairs singleton image is disjoint from the closed images of all other centres. A continuous obstacle in [-1,0], equal to -1 there and zero on those other images, exists by compact Hausdorff separation. On a second centre its unrestricted envelope is zero. On the first, G331's fixed-divisorial inequality g(nu)>=K g(w), K>0 independent of g and w, forces every minorant at the specified conductor-fibre point to be <=-1/K. Thus the separated raw envelope is not fibre constant, and the criterion excludes positive downstairs regularization. This does not classify internal fibres of one centre and does not prove anything impossible for the residual normal target.

# n9. Geometric curve envelopes and conventions

Use the entire qualified G331 and E350, and n1. For every excellent reduced local curve, its finite normalization has finitely many local DVR centres q. Away from the closed point it is the same generic field on each component. Thus S/R is supported only at the closed point, and its conductor contains a maximal-ideal power (or is the unit ideal). Every boundary point has finite conductor value, so every normalization fibre is singleton. The full link is the finite discrete set nu_q=ord_q/a_q, a_q=ord_q(a)>0; centres, not only minimal components, index its points.

On a DVR the actual closed-point Cartier divisor is effective and there are no contracted curve degree tests. Its arbitrary nonnegative real multiples give all finite nonpositive boundary constants; zero is the unit model. Semilocal finite products and G331's positive C-descent therefore prove C_R is EVERY finite nonpositive branch vector with genuine completed Cartier positivity. The finite vectors max(h,-N) decrease to every extended nonpositive vector h, proving D_R=[-infinity,0]^q by an actual representation. Only after this geometric membership proof does clipping give
\[
P_{geom}(phi)(q)=\min(phi(q),0)=P_{ideal}(phi)(q).
\]
This holds for every extended branch obstacle, including positive infinity, zero, mixed zero and partial bottom. Finite outputs are continuous; extended outputs are USC on this finite set. It is the complete ideal-envelope comparison through independently defined Cartier positivity, not an ideal-order completion renamed geometric.

Primary changes multiply branch coordinates by ord_q(a)/ord_q(b), exactly the one-factor cocycle, and commute with clipping. Qualified E350's curve reference is sum_q f_q a_q delta_nu_q with actual residue degrees f_q, including inseparability. Energy is the weighted sum of branch coordinates and is finite exactly for finite vectors; a bottom branch has positive reference mass. The smooth DVR is the one-point case, with maximal-ideal reference mass one. Dimension zero is empty and has zero measure/energy without negative arity. Nonpure lower-dimensional centres remain function and full-fibre data although ambient top-degree products can charge them zero. Nilpotents are reduced away and generic nilpotent intersection lengths are not reconstructed. Unsurjective arbitrary finite branch maps are not part of the normal dominating-cover theorem; bottom must remain available for their empty-fibre phenomena.

These valuative envelopes are distinct from literal logarithmic radial analytic extensions. At a complex two-disc node, the boundary vector (-1,0) is geometric here. A literal zero radial slope forces a common nodal value >=0 by USC; a negative slope on the other disc then conflicts with its maximum principle and outer value zero. The dossier's CLD radial assertion is retained as a scoped distinction, not used as a new general CLD theorem or as a reason to remove this geometric branch vector. No identification of general boundary traces with literal radial extensions is claimed.

# n10. Corrected graded and normal singular diagnostics

Use G331, B341 and E350 at their complete qualifications, and n1. These are universal mathematical diagnostics of proposed convergence arguments, followed by separately declared finite checks. They are NOT counterexamples to normal envelope existence for their chosen obstacles.

First let R=k[x,y]_(x,y), maximal-ideal gauge, over any field. J_j=(x,y^j), with J_0=R, is an ACTUAL graded family: J_r J_s is contained in J_(r+s), since the x-multiples are in (x) and the remaining product is y^(r+s). J_j contains m^j. Its primary core profile u_j=-min(v(x)/j,v(y)) increases to h=-1 at the unique support-(x) point q and zero elsewhere. For the latter assertion v(x) is finite off q; at q normalized y-order is one. Monomial weights (L,1) converge to q on all localized polynomials, while h has value zero at them. Thus h is not USC and not in D; h*=0 is in C. The continuous obstacle zero already has good envelope zero.

The exact all-r,s>=0 staircase count is
\[
\ell(R/m^r J_j^s)=r(r+1)/2+rs+j s(s+1)/2.
\]
For proof, product generators have exponents x=r+s-i-h, y=ji+h, with 0<=i<=s and 0<=h<=r. At an integer x-column 0<=x<r+s the smallest y is r+s-x+(j-1)max(0,s-x): substitute h=r+s-i-x and minimize the admissible i. Summing gives (r+s)(r+s+1)/2+(j-1)s(s+1)/2, the displayed formula, including r=0 or s=0. Comparing polynomial leading terms proves e(m,J_j)=1 and e(J_j)=j. B341/E350 give raw measure mass 1/j and
\[
F(u_j,u_j)=\int(-u_j)d\mu(u_j)=1/j,
\qquad E(u_j)=-1/(2j)\uparrow0.
\]
The positive quadratic form is B=F, NOT -F. The historical old354 positive-energy sign is explicitly rejected; its corrected body and mandatory sign annotation are retained unchanged. For any capacity test phi in D with -1<=phi<=0, E350's conditional Cauchy and scalar form order give F(u_j,phi)<=1/sqrt(j), because F(phi,phi)<=F(-1,-1)=1. Markov's inequality therefore proves Cap{u_j<-epsilon}<=1/(epsilon sqrt(j)). The raw measures converge in total variation to zero since their masses are 1/j. Capacity convergence to zero, correct energy maximization, and vanishing products do not make the exact increasing pointwise limit h a D-function.

Second let R=k[X,Y,Z]_(m)/(XY-Z^2)=k[s^2,st,t^2]_(m), over ANY field and in EVERY characteristic. Put M={(i,j) in Z^2:i+j even}. Its affine ring is k[M] intersect k[s,t] in k(s,t); both larger rings are normal, so the intersection is normal in its own fraction field. Localization preserves this. It is excellent, dimension two, cotangent dimension three and hence singular. At every boundary point a=v(X), b=v(Y), min(a,b)=1, and v(Z)=(a+b)/2 in the extended sense. The unique a=infinity point q kills (X,Z) and has Y-order one.

For I_n=(X^n,XY^(n-1),Y^(2n)), its primary core profile u_n=-v(I_n)/n is -1 when a<=b, and -min(1+(a-1)/n,2) when a>b finite; it is -2 at q. Again the n=1 generator is literally X. These functions increase in [-2,-1] to h=-1 off q and -2 at q. Semigroup monomial valuations with X-weight L, Y-weight one and Z-weight (L+1)/2 converge to q on all localized polynomials. Thus h is not USC and not D, while h*=-1 is already the good envelope of the obstacle -1.

The m-blowup is regular: the X and Y charts, with coordinates X,Z/X and Y,Z/Y, cover its exceptional conic XY=Z^2 even in characteristic two. Its generic exceptional DVR o has o(X)=o(Y)=o(Z)=1. The tautological restriction is O_conic(1), degree two. E350's actual geometric atom formula gives mu(-1)=2 delta_o. The function z=-v(X) belongs to D through the actual decreasing profiles -min(v(X),k)=-v((X)+m^k). Its finite reference moment is 2. E350 gives Cap{a>T}<=2/T and Cap{q}=0. The exact strict error set for 0<epsilon<1 is {(-1)-u_n>epsilon}={a>1+n epsilon}, so its capacity is <=2/(1+n epsilon). For epsilon>=1 it is empty. Even h is quasicontinuous, by deleting the genuine OPEN set {a>T}; nevertheless it is not in D. Exact all-support order cannot be replaced by capacity equality without another theorem.

Here is the UNIVERSAL multiplicity argument, independent of finite diagnostics. The exponents of the ring are the nonnegative even-parity lattice points. There are k^2 points of total degree less than 2k, giving ell(R/m^k)=k^2 and e(m)=2. For I_n the exponent generators are A=(2n,0), B=(2,2n-2), C=(0,4n). The bounded complement of their upward convex hull P is the polygon 0,A,B,C, of area 2n^2+2n; B=A at n=1. Exponents of I_n^k are contained in kP intersect M. Conversely express a lattice point in kP as an orthant remainder plus a convex combination of A,B,C with coefficients summing to k. Rounding the three coefficients down leaves at most two generators to add. A fixed shift (D,D), where D exceeds three times every generator coordinate, permits adding them while keeping a nonnegative even-parity remainder. Thus (kP intersect M)+(D,D) lies in Exp(I_n^k). Pure powers bound the missing points in a rectangle of side O(k); the difference between these two bounds lies in constant-width strips along finitely many edges, containing O(k) lattice points. Fixed-square tiling gives parity density one-half with boundary error O(k). Hence
\[
\ell(R/I_n^k)=(n^2+n)k^2+O(k),\qquad e(I_n)=2n^2+2n.
\]
The qualified form and energy satisfy F(u_n,u_n)=2+2/n and E(u_n)=-1-1/n increasing to E(-1)=-1. This is a bounded energy-maximizing sequence of minorants of -1 with a non-D exact limit, although its greatest envelope exists. Neither example refutes the surface theorem n5 or the original normal residual theorem.
